result.informal_description: For a Dirichlet character $ \chi $ modulo $ N $ and real number $ y $, if $ y \neq 0 $ or $ \chi $ is nontrivial, then the Dirichlet L-function $ L(\chi, s) $ evaluated at $ s = 1 + x + iy $ satisfies $ L(\chi, 1 + x + iy) = O(1) $ as $ x \to 0^+ $.

name: DirichletCharacter
LFunctionTrivChar
result.informal_name: Dirichlet L-function for the trivial character modulo $ N $
result.informal_description: The Dirichlet L-function associated with the trivial Dirichlet character modulo $ N $, which maps units in $ \mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z} $ to $ 1 $ and non-units to $ 0 $, defined as $ N^{-s} $ multiplied by the sum over all $ j \in \mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z} $ of $ \chi(j) $ times the Hurwitz zeta function $ \zeta(j/N, s) $.

name: EulerProduct
norm_tsum_factoredNumbers_sub_tsum_lt

result.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : NormedCommRing R] {f : ℕ → R} [CompleteSpace R],
  Summable f →

  obtain ⟨N, hN⟩ := summable_iff_nat_tsum_vanishing.mp hsum (Metric.ball 0 ε) <| Metric.ball_mem_nhds 0 εpos
  simp_rw [mem_ball_zero_iff] at hN
  refine ⟨N, fun s hs ↦ ?_⟩
  have := hN _ <| factoredNumbers_compl hs
  rwa [← hsum.tsum_subtype_add_tsum_subtype_compl (factoredNumbers s), add_sub_cancel_left,
    tsum_eq_tsum_diff_singleton (factoredNumbers s)ᶜ hf₀]
    -- Versions of the three lemmas above for `smoothNumbers N`
result.informal_name: Approximation of Total Sum by Sums Over Numbers with Bounded Prime Factors
result.informal_description: For any summable function $ f : \mathbb{N} \to E $ with $ f(0) = 0 $ and any $ \varepsilon > 0 $, there exists a natural number $ N $ such that for every finite set $ S \subseteq \mathbb{N} $ containing all primes less than $ N $, the norm of the difference between the total sum $ \sum_{m \in \mathbb{N}} f(m) $ and the sum over numbers with prime factors in $ S $ satisfies $ \left\| \sum_{m \in \mathbb{N}} f(m) - \sum_{m \in \text{factoredNumbers}(S)} f(m) \right\| < \varepsilon $. Here, $ \text{factoredNumbers}(S) $ denotes the set of nonzero natural numbers whose prime factors all belong to $ S $.

name: riemannZeta_eulerProduct_exp_log
result.signature: {s : ℂ} (hs : 1 < s.re) : exp (∑' p : Nat.Primes, -Complex.log (1 - p ^ (-s))) = riemannZeta s
result.type: ∀ {s : ℂ}, 1 < s.re → Complex.exp (∑' (p : Nat.Primes), -Complex.log (1 - ↑↑p ^ (-s))) = riemannZeta s
result.informal_name: Euler Product Formula for the Riemann Zeta Function via Exponential of Prime Logarithms
result.informal_description: For any complex number $ s $ with $ \operatorname{Re}(s) > 1 $, the exponential of the sum over all prime numbers $ p $ of $ -\log(1 - p^{-s}) $ equals the Riemann zeta function $ \zeta(s) $. That is, $ \exp\left(\sum_{p \in \mathbb{P}} -\log(1 - p^{-s})\right) = \zeta(s) $.

result.informal_description: For any natural number $ a $ that is a unit (i.e., $ a = 1 $), the infinite series $ \sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{\Lambda_{a}(n)}{n} $, where $ \Lambda_{a}(n) $ is defined as $ \Lambda(n) $ if $ n $ is prime and satisfies the residue class condition, and 0 otherwise, is not summable. name: DirichletCharacter
conductor
result.type: {R : Type u_1} → [inst : CommMonoidWithZero R] → {n : ℕ} → DirichletCharacter R n → ℕ
result.informal_description: The conductor of a Dirichlet character $\chi$ is the infimum of the conductor set of $\chi$, which consists of all natural numbers $d$ such that $\chi$ factors through the projection from $\mathbb{Z}/m\mathbb{Z}$ to $\mathbb{Z}/d\mathbb{Z}$, where $m$ is the modulus of $\chi$.

name: DirichletCharacter
conductorSet
result.type: {R : Type u_1} → [inst : CommMonoidWithZero R] → {n : ℕ} → DirichletCharacter R n → Set ℕ
result.informal_name: Conductor set of a Dirichlet character
result.informal_description: The set of natural numbers $ d $ for which the Dirichlet character $ \chi $ factors through the projection from $ \mathbb{Z}/m\mathbb{Z} $ to $ \mathbb{Z}/d\mathbb{Z} $, where $ m $ is the modulus of $ \chi $.

name: DirichletCharacter
factorsThrough_conductor
result.type: ∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : CommMonoidWithZero R] {n : ℕ} (χ : DirichletCharacter R n), χ.FactorsThrough χ.conductor
result.informal_name: Dirichlet Character Factors Through Its Conductor
result.informal_description: For a Dirichlet character $\chi$ modulo $m$, the character $\chi$ factors through the canonical projection from $\mathbb{Z}/m\mathbb{Z}$ to $\mathbb{Z}/d\mathbb{Z}$, where $d$ is the conductor of $\chi$. This means $\chi$ agrees with a Dirichlet character modulo $d$ on elements coprime to $m$.

result.informal_name: Conductor of Dirichlet Character is in Conductor Set
result.informal_description: The conductor $ d $ of a Dirichlet character $ \chi $ is an element of its conductor set, i.e., $ d \in \text{conductorSet}(\chi) $.

name: DirichletCharacter
level_mem_conductorSet

result.informal_name: The modulus of a Dirichlet character is in its conductor set
result.informal_description: For a Dirichlet character $\chi$ modulo $n$, the modulus $n$ belongs to the conductor set of $\chi$, which consists of all natural numbers $d$ such that $\chi$ factors through the canonical projection $\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{Z}/d\mathbb{Z}$.
